'''Mountain Warehouse Limited''' is a British [[Outdoor recreation|outdoor]] retailer selling equipment for [[hiking]], [[camping]], [[skiing]], [[cycling]], [[running]] and fitness.

Founded in 1997 by Mark Neale, Mountain Warehouse has grown from a single outlet store to over 330 stores in the [[UK]], [[Europe]], [[New Zealand]] and [[North America]].

==History==
In 1997, Mountain Warehouse was founded as the retail partner of [[Karrimor|Karrimor International]], the UK based outdoor clothing and equipment manufacturer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.investindustrial.com/en/investments/mountain-warehouse |title=Mountain Warehouse |accessdate=10 March 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140310214236/http://www.investindustrial.com/en/investments/mountain-warehouse |archivedate=10 March 2014 }}</ref> Investment company 21 Invest (now Investindustrial) were Karrimor's lead investor.

21 Invest sold Karrimor's core business to [[South Africa]]n leisure group Cullinan Holdings in February 1999.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.inov8.au.com/compass/karrimorhistory.html |title=Karrimor History |accessdate=16 August 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140310224950/http://www.inov8.au.com/compass/karrimorhistory.html |archivedate=10 March 2014 }}</ref> The stores, which were initially branded Karrimor, were subsequently re-branded to Mountain Warehouse. Under the new name, Mountain Warehouse began selling multi-branded outdoor clothing and equipment as well as its recently launched own brand of clothing.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nbgipe.com/uk/investments/realised-investments/investment-detail/items/mountain-warehouse |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140310200521/http://www.nbgipe.com/uk/investments/realised-investments/investment-detail/items/mountain-warehouse |url-status=dead |archive-date=10 March 2014 |title=NBGI Private Equity "NBGI PE" - Investment detail |website=Nbgipe.com |date= |accessdate=16 June 2016 }}</ref>

In August 2002, NBGI Private Equity acquired the business from 21 Invest and managing Director Mark Neale, buying a majority stake in the company. CEO Neale reinvested most of his proceeds into the new acquisition. In the years that NBGI worked with Mountain Warehouse, their [[own brand]] product offering increased from 5% to 80%.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=http://www.unquote.com/uk/official-record/2304651/ldc-sells-mountain-warehouse-to-management |title=LDC sells Mountain Warehouse to management |website=Unquote.com |date=4 November 2013 |accessdate=16 June 2016}}</ref>

In July 2007, Mountain Warehouse management around Neale bought out NBGI Private Equity for £15m, backed by Icelandic investment fund KCAJ.<ref name="thecourier1"/>

In August 2010, the private-equity arm of [[Lloyds Banking Group]], LDC, took a 23% minority stake in the business as part of another £47m buyout by Mountain Warehouse management.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.growthbusiness.co.uk/news-and-market-deals/mergers-and-acquisitions/2428557/mountain-warehouse-ends-private-equity-backing-and-takes-full-control.thtml |title=Mountain Warehouse ends private equity backing and takes full control |website=Growthbusiness.co.uk |date=4 November 2013 |accessdate=16 June 2016}}</ref>

In November 2013, the management team led by founder and CEO Mark Neale bought out minority shareholder LDC to take full ownership of the retail chain. Mr Neale personally owns 85% of the business. The £85m deal was backed by the [[Royal Bank of Scotland]] and asset management firm Alcentra.<ref name="telegraph1">{{cite web|last=Ruddick |first=Graham |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/retailandconsumer/10423813/Mountain-Warehouse-peaks-at-85m.html |title=Mountain Warehouse peaks at £85m |publisher=Telegraph |date= 3 November 2013|accessdate=16 June 2016}}</ref>

In 2015, Mountain Warehouse Holdings Limited set up a new company, ‘Zakti Activeware’, which was the new name for ‘Mountain Warehouse Active’ range, and transferred a lot of stock to the new stores. They were closed in 2018,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowden |first=Grace |date=8 October 2018 |title=Mountain Warehouse abandons Zakti store format {{!}} News {{!}} Retail Week |url=https://www.retail-week.com/sports-and-leisure/mountain-warehouse-abandons-zakti-store-format/7030059.article?authent=1 |website=Retail Week}}</ref> and the website now redirects to their 'Active People' range.

In 2018, Mountain Warehouse Holdings Limited set up another new company ‘Neon Sheep’ to break into the gifts and accessories market, but these stores were closed in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2 July 2022 |title=Swindonian readers upset over Neon Sheep closing down at Outlet |url=https://theswindonian.co.uk/news/swindonian-readers-upset-over-neon-sheep-closing-down-at-outlet/ |access-date=20 July 2025 |website=Swindonian}}</ref>

In 2021 fashion retailer Animal was acquired<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-28 |title=Mountain Warehouse introduces Animal to its offerings {{!}} Retail News UK |url=https://apparelresources.com/business-news/retail/mountain-warehouse-introduces-animal-offerings/ |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=Apparel Resources |language=en-US}}</ref> for previous owner H Young Holdings launching it online in the same year. By 2024, Animal stores were reopening.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-05 |title=Mountain Warehouse confirms closure of Norwich store |url=https://www.eveningnews24.co.uk/news/24632285.mountain-warehouse-store-norwich-become-animal/ |access-date=2025-12-15 |website=Norwich Evening News |language=en}}</ref>

On September 3, 2024, Mountain Warehouse acquired the US-based retailer [[Eastern Mountain Sports]] for $10 million.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://www.ctinsider.com/business/article/ct-ems-danbury-meriden-waterford-bobs-mountain-19738981.php|website=ctinsider.com|title=Eastern Mountain Sports stores in CT purchased by UK-based Mountain Warehouse|date=2024-09-03|access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref>

==Stores==
[[File:Ex-WoolworthsKeswick.JPG|thumb|A Mountain Warehouse store in [[Keswick, Cumbria|Keswick]], [[Cumbria]]]]
Mountain Warehouse has over 400 stores in the UK, North America, Europe and New Zealand, including stores in [[Dublin, Ireland]], [[Vienna, Austria]], and stores in [[Poland]] including [[Warsaw]].

The first Mountain Warehouse store opened in 1997. By August 2002 Mountain Warehouse had opened a further 13 stores in factory outlet centres in the UK and one in Vienna, as well as three concession stores in UK [[garden centre]]s.

The London [[Covent Garden]] store was the first of Mountain Warehouse's high street stores. By 2019 Mountain Warehouse opened a further 9 stores in London, located in popular areas such as [[Regent Street]], [[Fulham]] and [[Wimbledon, London|Wimbledon]].

Mountain Warehouse purchased six of former [[Woolworths (United Kingdom)|Woolworths]] sites,<ref>{{cite web|last=Wallop |first=Harry |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/newsbysector/retailandconsumer/9022600/What-happened-to-all-the-Woolworths-shops.html |title=What happened to all the Woolworths shops? |publisher=Telegraph |date= 19 January 2012|accessdate=16 June 2016}}</ref> including [[Fort William, Highland|Fort William, Scotland]],<ref name="thecourier1">{{cite web |title=Mountain Warehouse under new ownership |url=https://homeofdirectcommerce.com/news/mountain-warehouse-under-new-ownership/ |archiveurl= |archivedate= |accessdate=27 September 2022 |website=directcommerce.com|date=9 October 2007 }}</ref> [[St Ives, Cornwall]]<ref>{{cite web|last=Soult |first=Graham |url=http://www.soultsretailview.co.uk/2011/09/21/the-new-occupants-of-cornwalls-ex-woolies-plus-one-thats-still-empty |title=The new occupants of Cornwall's ex-Woolies - plus one that's still empty - Soult's Retail View |website=Soultsretailview.co.uk |date= 21 September 2011|accessdate=16 June 2016}}</ref> and [[Buxton|Buxton, Derbyshire]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.buxtonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local/woolies-new-life-1-651144 |title=Woolies' new life |publisher=[[Buxton Advertiser]] |date=19 March 2009 |accessdate=16 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160809180720/http://www.buxtonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local/woolies-new-life-1-651144 |archive-date=9 August 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Mountain Warehouse has continued to secure premises in market towns and locations popular with walkers and holidaymakers.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ldc.co.uk/news/new-heights-for-mountain-warehouse-following-management-buy-back.aspx |title=News |website=LDC.co.uk |date= |accessdate=16 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151030050920/http://www.ldc.co.uk/news/new-heights-for-mountain-warehouse-following-management-buy-back.aspx |archive-date=30 October 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 9 March 2024, Mountain Warehouse opened its largest UK store yet on Boscawen Street in Truro, Cornwall.

Mountain Warehouse opened its first North America outlet store in [[Toronto|Toronto, Ontario]], Canada early 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.retail-insider.com/retail-insider/tail-insider.com/2014/01/mountain-warehouse-to-expand-into-canada.html |title=Mountain Warehouse to further expand into Canada |website=Retail-insider.com |date=15 January 2014 |accessdate=16 June 2016}}</ref> It has since further expanded to other North American locations including [[New Jersey, United States]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bizjournals.com/pittsburgh/news/2014/05/19/new-outdoors-retailer-coming-to-grove-city-premium.html|title=New outdoors retailer coming to Grove City Premium Outlets|website=Bizjournals.com|accessdate=16 June 2016}}</ref> [[Burlington, Ontario|Burlington]], Canada<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mapleviewcentre.com/stores/equipment-clothing-nutrition-burlington/mountain-warehouse/ |title=Mapleview Mall Directory |website=www.mapleviewcentre.com}}</ref> and [[Vancouver]], Canada.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mountainwarehouse.com/stores/canada/vancouver-mcarthurglen/ |title=Store Locator |website=Mountainwarehouse.com |date= |accessdate=16 June 2016}}</ref>

Mountain Warehouse's headquarters are located in [[Victoria, London]]. A store is also located nearby in Victoria Place in [[London Victoria station]].

==Products==
Mountain Warehouse has grown from a stock clearance business selling only [[Brand|branded products]] to a business that sells mainly [[own brand]] [[clothing]], [[footwear]] and equipment.<ref>{{cite web|last=White |first=Dominic |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/finance/markets/2812004/Mountain-Warehouse-buyout.html |title=Mountain Warehouse buyout |publisher=Telegraph |date=12 July 2007 |accessdate=16 June 2016}}</ref> In 2004 own brands including Mountain Life, Parallel and Snapdragon made up 10% of the business's products but by 2007 own brand products made up 65%.<ref name="telegraph1"/>

In 2010 the retailer introduced a more technical clothing range, Mountainlife Extreme. The Mountainlife Extreme clothing range was designed to compete with higher end brands such as [[The North Face]] and [[Berghaus]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ldc.co.uk/News/LDC-private-equity-buys-significant-stake-in-outdoor-specialist-Mountain-Warehouse.aspx |title=News |website=Ldc.co.uk |date= |accessdate=16 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140310214250/http://www.ldc.co.uk/News/LDC-private-equity-buys-significant-stake-in-outdoor-specialist-Mountain-Warehouse.aspx |archive-date=10 March 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The Mountainlife and Parallel branding has gradually been phased out with all clothing, footwear and equipment now branded with Mountain Warehouse. Mountainlife Extreme was replaced by Mountain Warehouse Extreme, with footwear, accessories and equipment also included in the range.

Mountain Warehouse Limited is a British outdoor retailer selling equipment for hiking, camping, skiing, cycling, running and fitness.
Founded in 1997 by Mark Neale, Mountain Warehouse has grown from a single outlet store to over 330 stores in the UK, Europe, New Zealand and North America.
